raw.notes: Clone: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-matthew-circuits-com/1a91b583-5ce8-47da-87b4-dd08761fbeb2/scratchpad/alias-harvest/kicad-jlcpcb-tools (depth-1, HEAD). Key facts: (1) The symbol/footprint LCSC alias is a REGEX, not a list — footprint_helpers.get_lcsc_value accepts ANY field whose name matches re.match(r"lcsc|jlc", name, re.IGNORECASE) (prefix match, so 'LCSC', 'lcsc', 'LCSC Part #', 'JLCPCB', 'JLC_PN' all hit) AND whose VALUE matches ^C\\d+$ — the value grammar is half the detector. When writing back it reuses the existing field's name, else creates literally "LCSC" (hidden). (2) schematicexport.py (KiCad 8+ path) hardcodes the set {"LCSC","LCSC_PN","JLC_PN"} for schematic properties; the KiCad 6 and 7 paths (lines 77, 152) accept only "LCSC". New properties are always written as "LCSC". (3) The JLCPCB BOM header written by fabrication.generate_bom is exactly: Comment,Designator,Footprint,LCSC,Quantity. The CPL/placement header is: Designator,Val,Package,Mid X,Mid Y,Rotation,Layer. (4) 'LCSC Part' / 'MFR.Part' / 'Library Type' / 'First Category' / 'Second Category' / 'Solder Joint' are JLCPCB parts-DATABASE (sqlite/CSV) column names used for search + the partmapper export header, not symbol fields.

raw.notes:
Clone: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-matthew-circuits-com/1a91b583-5ce8-47da-87b4-dd08761fbeb2/scratchpad/alias-harvest/kibom (shallow, github.com/SchrodingersGat/KiBoM). Paths above are repo-relative to that clone.

Direction nuance: the columns.py constants are simultaneously (a) the default BOM output headers via _COLUMNS_DEFAULT (kibom/columns.py:29-41) and (b) names matched case-insensitively when pulling data off a component — kibom/component.py:282-316 special-cases each one against intrinsic netlist data, and kibom/component.py:319-321 ("# Other fields (case insensitive)" / "for f in self.getFieldNames(): if f.lower() == name.lower():") is the ONLY generic symbol-field lookup. That single case-fold is the entirety of KiBoM's "alias" tolerance: any column name a user adds is matched to a symbol field by lowercase equality, nothing more.

The thing named "aliases" in this repo is NOT a field-name table. [COMPONENT_ALIASES] (kibom/preferences.py:23 SECTION_ALIASES = "COMPONENT_ALIASES"; defaults at kibom/preferences.py:114-121) lists equivalent SYMBOL NAME VALUES for grouping: ["c", "c_small", "cap", "capacitor"], ["r", "r_small", "res", "resistor"], ["sw", "switch"], ["l", "l_small", "inductor"], ["zener", "zenersmall"], ["d", "diode", "d_small"] — cell values in the Part column, consumed at kibom/component.py:86-87. Reported as notes, not as aliases, since they are not field/column names.

Likewise the DNF/DNC lists (kibom/component.py:14-28 and 31-36) are VALUES a fit field may hold, not field names: DNF = "dnf","dnl","dnp","do not fit","do not place","do not load","nofit","nostuff","noplace","noload","not fitted","not loaded","not placed","no stuff"; DNC = "dnc","do not change","no change","fixed". Note "dnp" appears in BOTH senses — as a DNF cell value (component.py:17) and as a KiCad 7 property NAME (component.py:359).

Column renaming is user-driven only: SECTION_COLUMN_RENAME = "COLUMN_RENAME" (kibom/preferences.py:28) maps a column to a display name at write time (csv_writer.py:48-49); it ships empty (self.colRename = {} at preferences.py:98).

Default ignored columns are 'Part Lib' / 'Footprint Lib' (preferences.py:55-59; test/bom.ini:39-40); default grouping fields are Part, Part Lib, Value, Footprint, Footprint Lib (preferences.py:88-94).

JACKPOT: kicost/edas/eda.py:35-90 is an explicit alias/synonym dictionary `field_name_translations` mapping lowercased user spellings -> KiCost canonical field names. Lookups are case-INSENSITIVE: every call lowercases+strips first (eda.py:178 `f = f.lower().strip()`; generic_csv.py:165 `hdr.strip().lower()`). The SAME table is applied to BOTH symbol fields (eda.py:181 in eda_class.process_fields) and CSV BOM column headers (generic_csv.py:165) — I tagged table entries `reads_symbol_field` because that module owns them, but each is equally a BOM-column alias.

Distributor part-number fields are GENERATED, not literal (eda.py:92-97): for each distributor slug in {arrow, digikey, farnell, mouser, newark, rs, tme, lcsc} (distributors_info.py:63-113) and each stub in ['part#','#','p#','pn','vendor#','vp#','vpn','num'], the table gains `<dist><stub>`, `<dist>_<stub>` and `<dist>-<stub>` -> `<dist>#`. So 'digikey#', 'digikeypart#', 'digikey_pn', 'mouser-vpn' all normalize to 'digikey#'/'mouser#'. I report canonical generated forms plus the generating lines rather than enumerating ~200 combinations.

Other conventions: `kicost:FIELD` and `kicost.VARIANT:FIELD` prefixed fields override plain ones (eda.py:196-209); `DISTRIBUTOR:FIELD` (SEPRTR=':') scopes a field to one distributor (eda.py:127-144); bare 'cat#', 'pricing', 'link' auto-assign to the 'Local' distributor (eda.py:156-158). Per-part quantity uses 'manf#_qty' and '<dist>#_qty' (kicost.py:197).

Headerless-CSV fallback (generic_csv.py:186-190): 1 col => manf#; 2 cols => manf#, refs; 3+ => qty, manf#, refs.

DISTRIBUTOR PN NAMES ARE COMPOSED, NOT LITERAL. kibot/misc.py:161-164 defines DISTRIBUTORS (8 names), DISTRIBUTORS_STUBS (8 stubs) and DISTRIBUTORS_STUBS_SEPS = '_- '. The cross-product is built at kibot/out_bom.py:1238-1244: `dpn_set.add(dist+stub)` and, when stub != '#', `dpn_set.add(dist+sep+stub)`. So the recognized set is e.g. digikey#, digikey_part#, digikey-pn, mouser vpn, lcsc num, etc. — 8 dists x (1 + 7x3) = 176 names, all lowercase. I reported the literal component strings only; do not treat 'arrow'/'part#' alone as a column name. Same cross-product drives LCSC autodiscovery at kibot/optionable.py:663-672, with bare 'lcsc' (line 674) and hard fallback 'LCSC#' (lines 658, 695).

DEFAULT COLUMN SET (written): kibot/bom/columnlist.py:105-120 COLUMNS_DEFAULT = Row, Description, Part, Part Lib, References, Value, Footprint, Footprint Lib, Quantity Per PCB, Build Quantity, Status, Datasheet, Sheetpath, Source BoM. COLUMNS_EXTRA (lines 135-154) is the not-by-default set (the ${...} KiCad attrs, footprint XYRS, net columns). COLUMNS_PROTECTED_L (157-184) are immutable names — note line 158 makes both 'reference' and 'references' protected, and kibot/out_bom.py:787-791 explicitly rewrites a user's 'Reference' column to 'References'.

DEFAULT GROUPING KEYS: kibot/bom/columnlist.py:187-193 DEFAULT_GROUPING = part, part lib, value, footprint, footprint lib (lowercase); kibot/out_bom.py:446 extends it with 'voltage','tolerance','current','power'; the KiBoM-compat output repeats it TitleCased at kibot/out_kibom.py:108 `_default = ['Part', 'Part Lib', 'Value', 'Footprint', 'Footprint Lib']`.

DNP VALUE VOCABULARY (values, not field names — so not listed as aliases): kibot/misc.py:137-151 DNF = {dnf, dnl, dnp, do not fit, do not place, do not load, nofit, nostuff, noplace, noload, not fitted, not loaded, not placed, no stuff}; kibot/misc.py:154-158 DNC = {dnc, do not change, no change, fixed}. These are matched against the value of the field named by fil_generic.py:46 `self.config_field = 'Config'`.

Value-joining property fields (kibot/globals.py:153-174) each ship a 2-entry default alias list; kibot/out_bom.py:1260 intersects the schematic's fields with {'tolerance','voltage','power','current'}.

raw.notes:
Clone: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-matthew-circuits-com/1a91b583-5ce8-47da-87b4-dd08761fbeb2/scratchpad/alias-harvest/fabrication-toolkit (depth 1, default branch). All aliases live in one file, plugins/process.py.

JACKPOT TABLE — _get_mpn_from_footprint (plugins/process.py:461-473) is the JLC/LCSC part-number alias resolver. It is built as a CROSS PRODUCT, so the 12 combined names above do not appear as string literals; they are generated at line 465 from these literals:
  463: supplier_names = ['LCSC', 'JLCPCB']
  464: pn_abbrevs = ['Part #', 'Part', 'PN', 'P/N', 'Part No.', 'Part Number']
  465: keys = [(sn + " " + abr) for sn in supplier_names for abr in pn_abbrevs]
  466: fallback_keys = ['LCSC', 'JLC', 'MPN', 'Mpn', 'mpn']
Precedence is list order: all 12 "<supplier> <abbrev>" combos first (LCSC before JLCPCB, abbrevs in the order listed), then the 5 bare fallbacks. First non-empty wins (471-473). A footprint carrying a field literally named 'dnp' short-circuits to the string 'DNP' (468-469) before any part-number lookup.

Field lookup is name-based across KiCad API generations via plugins/utils.py:48-66 (HasField / HasFieldByName / HasProperty), i.e. exact-string, case-SENSITIVE matching — hence the explicit MPN/Mpn/mpn triple.

BOM WRITE SCHEMA — bom.csv (config.py:8 bomFileName = 'bom.csv'), header row emitted from the first dict's keys (process.py:312 csv_writer.writerow(self.bom[0].keys())), so column order is exactly the insertion order at 284-291:
  Designator, Footprint, Quantity, Value, LCSC Part #
Encoding utf-8-sig (BOM-prefixed UTF-8), plain csv.writer. A commented-out 'Mount' column sits at line 289. Merge/dedup key is Footprint + Value(upper) + 'LCSC Part #' with Quantity < bomRowLimit (200, config.py:11); merged rows join designators with ", " (277).

Companion positions.csv (config.py:7 placementFileName), same header-from-keys mechanism (299), columns from process.py:253-259: Designator, Mid X, Mid Y, Rotation, Layer. Reported here for completeness only — it is a placement file, not a BOM.

raw.notes:
Line numbers for HTML sources are line numbers in the firecrawl --only-main-content markdown render of that URL (saved under the session scratchpad), not in the raw HTML; quotes are verbatim from that render including its markdown escaping (e.g. "\\-"). Line numbers for bom.ulp and the CSV are true file line numbers.

JLCPCB: the help page enumerates only Comment / Designator / Footprint as the mandatory fields; the downloadable "JLC Sample BOM" XLSX (linked from that page) has a 4-column header row A1..D1 whose D1 is rich text "JLCPCB Part #" + "（optional）" — the literal token is "JLCPCB Part #". The "Recommendations for BOM / CPL File Preparation" page says "Please modify the column headers in your files to match the standard field names recognized by our system" but publishes NO alias/synonym table — no jackpot table was found for any of the five tools.

Mouser: "Mouser Part Number" and "Manufacturer Part Number" are mapping TARGETS in the FORTE BOM tool's column-mapping step ("At least one of the following options must be mapped"), not headers Mouser writes.

Digi-Key: the five aliases sourced from raw.githubusercontent.com/im-tomu/tomu-hardware are the header row of a file named bom-digikey.csv in a third-party hardware repo — it has the shape of a Digi-Key BOM Manager/list export, but I could NOT confirm Digi-Key generated it, so direction is "unknown" and it must not be treated as an attested vendor template. The only Digi-Key-attested string is "Customer Reference".

Altium: reported strings are dialog/report column names, quoted verbatim from Altium's own documentation; the surrounding section is BOM Comparison. Treat with the caveat above.

EAGLE bom.ulp emits two different header rows depending on list type: Parts list (line 378) = Part / Value / Device / Package / Description, Values list (line 403) = Qty / Value / Device / Package / Parts / Description. Both are wrapped in tr() so a localized EAGLE emits translated headers (the German catalog at lines 113-117 shows "Bauteil\tWert\tDevice\tPackage\tDescription" and "Menge\tWert\tDevice\tGehäuse\tBauteile").
